overall: Atlanta reached a daily high of 91.4°F around 16:19 ET, well above NWP model forecasts, before a line of severe thunderstorms swept through the region causing a sharp ~9°F outflow-driven temperature crash to 80.6°F by 17:52 ET. By 19:00 ET, temperatures had partially recovered to 82.4°F but with multiple active severe thunderstorm warnings and a tornado warning in the area, further significant warming is essentially impossible. The day ran notably hotter than models anticipated in the peak afternoon hours.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models undershot today's observed peak substantially — ECMWF at 87.5°F, NBM at 86.8°F, and even the warmest model HRRR at 90.1°F all came in below the already-locked-in running max of 91.4°F. The convective environment destabilized more aggressively ahead of the storm line than models captured, allowing afternoon heating to push temperatures higher before the severe weather arrived and collapsed the boundary layer.
max_temp_prediction: Today's TMAX is effectively locked in at 91.4°F — the running max has been stationary at that value since 17:00 ET, the give-up classifier fired at hour 14.67 with 91% probability, and it is now 19:00 ET with severe thunderstorm activity actively suppressing temperatures. The INTRADAY model shows 96.8% probability in the 90–91.9°F bucket, consistent with the observed 91.4°F peak. There is negligible chance of the running max being exceeded tonight. Confidence is very high.
